audit_findings.title: A negative trough-year anchor is being grown into perpetuity
audit_findings.magnitude: Computed adjustment to the limited-liability floor is $4,832.0-$8,096.0 million, or $14.98-$25.09 per share; normalized value is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The negative $646.6 million OE anchor flows through forecast growth and terminal value, making every operating PV negative and making higher growth reduce value.
audit_findings.evidence: For the year ended December 31, 2025, net cash provided by operating activities was $0.8 billion, compared to $1.3 billion in the prior year.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated economic-sign error. Capitalizing a negative cyclical observation forever produces negative common-equity values even though 2025 operating cash flow was $824.8 million. The resulting per-share outputs are not usable estimates of common equity value. A zero floor fixes the limited-liability violation but does not determine normalized earning power.
audit_findings.action: Separate cyclical and investment effects, estimate normalized maintenance-capital OE from filed multi-year data, rerun all scenarios, and floor common equity value at zero.

audit_findings.title: Consolidated cash-flow inputs may not match the parent-only share denominator
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified (25% of Miski Mayo and 38% of Fospar are outside parent ownership; filed 2025 NCI earnings were $34.7 million)
audit_findings.mechanism: Consolidated operating cash flow, capital expenditure, working capital and cash may include subsidiary amounts belonging to NCI, while value is divided solely among Mosaic parent shares.
audit_findings.evidence: We have a 75% economic interest in the Miski Mayo Mine and consolidate its results.
audit_findings.explanation: The ownership mismatch is a demonstrated possibility, but the record does not establish the dollar error. Subtracting NCI earnings does not necessarily remove the NCI share of cash-flow and bridge components. Subsidiary-level cash flows and capital spending are not supplied, so neither direction nor materiality can be established.
audit_findings.action: Build a parent-attributable schedule for Miski Mayo, Fospar and every other consolidated non-wholly-owned subsidiary, covering operating cash flow, maintenance capital, working capital, cash, liabilities and distributions; then rerun OE and the bridge.

audit_findings.title: Total capital expenditure may have been mistaken for maintenance capital
audit_findings.magnitude: $1,359.4 million of 2025 total capital expenditure against $824.8 million of operating cash flow; maintenance-versus-growth adjustment unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Deducting expansion and discretionary investment as maintenance capital directly depresses anchor OE and every forecast and terminal-value cash flow.
audit_findings.evidence: In 2025, we completed construction of a one million tonne distribution facility in northern Brazil in Palmeirante.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that total capital spending included investment activity, including completion of the one-million-tonne Palmeirante distribution facility. The valuation's $646.6 million OE loss is therefore potentially an artifact of deducting total rather than maintenance capital. The filing does not disclose the facility's cost or a complete maintenance/growth split, so the correction cannot yet be quantified.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $1,359.4 million capital-expenditure total by project into sustaining, replacement, mandatory environmental and growth categories; deduct only capital required to preserve normal volume and competitive position, then rerun every scenario.

audit_findings.title: The ARO claim is not explicitly reconciled to future owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $2,601.9 million present-value ARO at 2025-12-31 versus $743.3 million of restricted RCRA trusts, a gross difference of $1,858.6 million before scope and timing reconciliation
audit_findings.mechanism: Future reclamation, closure and water-treatment cash settlements must either reduce normalized OE as paid or enter the equity bridge as an uncovered claim; restricted trust assets cannot be treated as freely distributable value.
audit_findings.evidence: The corresponding present value of all future expenditures is $2.6 billion as of December 31, 2025 and is reflected in our accrued liabilities and other noncurrent liabilities in our Consolidated Balance Sheets.
audit_findings.explanation: The obligation and its scale are demonstrated, but omission is not yet proven because current ARO settlements may already pass through operating cash flow. The valuation does not show that forecast OE captures the full settlement profile or that an uncovered liability was included in the bridge. The gross ARO is about four times the $646.6 million anchor loss and exceeds the $1,755.1 million positive stakes bridge, so the treatment is capable of materially changing a normalized valuation.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each ARO category's projected cash settlements to normalized OE, identify amounts already captured, match restricted trusts only to obligations they legally secure, and include any remaining uncovered claim exactly once in a rerun.

audit_findings.title: The anchor includes production from a business already sold
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified operating contribution; filed consideration was up to $111 million for Patos de Minas, $27 million for Taquari and approximately $30 million for Carlsbad
audit_findings.mechanism: Cash flows from disposed operations remain in 2025 anchor OE even though those operations will not contribute prospectively; sale proceeds or receivables may also require one-time bridge treatment.
audit_findings.evidence: The 2025 amounts represent production from the beginning of the year until the selling date of November 4, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated: Taquari contributed production through November 4, 2025, Patos de Minas was sold in October 2025, and Carlsbad closed on April 30, 2026. Materiality and direction remain unresolved because the filing does not provide stand-alone owner earnings for these operations; removing a profitable operation lowers value, while removing a cash-consuming operation raises it.
audit_findings.action: Prepare continuing-perimeter OE for Taquari, Patos de Minas and Carlsbad using operation-level cash flow and maintenance capital; reconcile cash, deferred and contingent consideration and ensure each item enters the bridge exactly once.

audit_findings.title: The Ma’aden stake may not be worth unrestricted quoted market value to Mosaic today
audit_findings.magnitude: $1,755.1 million, or $5.44 per diluted share and 21.0% of the $25.85 market price; restriction and tax adjustment unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds the quoted Ma’aden stake as a separate asset, while transfer restrictions, delayed monetization and taxes may reduce realizable proceeds; retaining related dividends or mark-to-market gains in OE would double count the asset.
audit_findings.evidence: The shares received by Mosaic are subject to transfer and sale restrictions, which will be released over a five-year period.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filed Ma’aden carrying value exactly equals the $1,755.1 million stakes bridge, demonstrating that essentially the full quoted value was added. The shares are released from transfer restrictions over five years, but the record supplies no restriction or tax adjustment. The size of the stake makes even a moderate haircut capable of affecting a normalized valuation. Whether the $317.4 million 2025 unrealized gain was retained in OE remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the contractual release schedule and tax basis, calculate a present-value marketability and tax adjustment, and reconcile all Ma’aden dividends, interest and unrealized gains out of operating OE before rerunning the bridge.
